title: Development and Evaluation of a Modular Group Therapy Program for Treating Sexuality-Related Problems Following Interpersonal Violence in an Inpatient and Day Clinic DBT-Setting (DBT-Sex): A Pilot Study
summary: Sexuality-related difficulties are common in patients with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and borderline personality disorder (BPD) following interpersonal (sexual) violence (Bird et al., 2021, Sansone & Sansone, 2011), but are rarely treated systematically in everyday clinical practice. Studies show that even after successful trauma-focused treatment, symptoms such as sexual avoidance, shame, self-harming sexual behaviour or high-risk behaviour often persist in women with PTSD (Haase et al., 2009; O'Driscoll & Flanagan, 2016). Initial group programmes in sex therapy suggest that specifically addressing these issues can improve symptoms (Brotto et al., 2012; Chudakov et al., 2008). However, there is currently a lack of manualised group programmes that specifically address sexuality-related problems in patients with trauma-related disorders in DBT-oriented inpatient and day clinic settings. The present study aims to contribute to the further development of a practical group programme in an inpatient and day clinic DBT context and to specifically contribute to the improvement of sexuality-related symptoms in patients with post-traumatic stress disorder.
conditions: Sexual dysfunctions, Trauma-associated sexual problems, (complex) Posttraumatic stress disorder, Borderline personality disorder (BPD)

interventions.name: Intervention: A Modular Group Therapy Program for Treating Sexuality-Related Problems Following Interpersonal Violence in an Inpatient and Day Clinic DBT-Setting (DBT-Sex) within four structured modules

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of (complex) PTSD or BPD
- Ongoing inpatient or day-clinic DBT treatment
- Sex/gender: female (cisgender woman); in individual cases, non-binary persons assigned female at birth who experience their female genitals as congruent
- Participation in a preliminary interview to assess suitability for the group
- Signed informed consent for study participation and data collection
- History of interpersonal violence
- Sexuality-related problems: avoidance behavior, self-injurious sexual behavior, dissociation during sex, high-risk sexual behavior, trauma-associated emotions and cognitions
- Sufficient capacity for self-regulation during intrusive and dissociative experiences
Exclusion criteria:
- Ongoing contact with the perpetrator
- Current violent relationship
- Psychotic symptoms
- Severe self-injurious behavior
- Acute suicidality
- Regular and heavy use of drugs, alcohol, or sedatives
(As all patients are embedded in the existing treatment program, these exclusion criteria are checked prior to participation.)
